source.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
source.authors: J. Barron; Dan Gnanapragasam; Michael Tschannen

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests whether softmax numerical errors affect grokking: it compares standard and corrected cross-entropy and reports numerical-instability spikes, test-accuracy changes, and grokking outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper's own algorithmic-training results are included below. It also discusses prior grokking results, which are not recorded as findings of this study. The zero-sum projection and StableMax comparisons are omitted: they are alternative methods, not results for the standard or corrected cross-entropy that bears on V7. Soft-target distillation results do not measure grokking.
record.test_reason: The study runs standard grokking benchmarks (modular arithmetic, 1-layer Transformers, 2-layer MLPs) with and without a fix for the softmax floating-point bug. It compares precision and Adam ε and reports test accuracy and slingshot spikes. This directly probes whether numerical choices produce or alter grokking dynamics (V7). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Softmax Collapse causes slingshot spikes that slow and hurt grokking with weight decay and collapse accuracy without it. Their fix removes the spikes, speeds up grokking, and reveals margins converging to log(1/ε). They do not claim grokking itself is a numerical artifact.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments reuse modular-grokking benchmark settings but change the softmax/cross-entropy implementation and compare floating-point precision and optimizer epsilon; this is not a reproduction of the original grokking training recipe as a whole.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with loss implementation, logit precision, Adam epsilon, weight decay, and benchmark/task; standard cross-entropy fails at precision cliffs in some settings, while corrected cross-entropy crosses them smoothly.

fits_no_version.finding: The fixed CE eliminates slingshot loss spikes. Standard fp32 CE spikes at c32≈16.6 on all four benchmarks, and bf16 stalls at c16≈5.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slingshot loss spikes during grokking are caused by Softmax Collapse interacting with Adam's second moment.

fits_no_version.finding: Under AdamW with weight decay, logit margins after memorization settle at about log(1/ε) (Fig. 4, Table 1 margins).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The post-memorization margin is bounded by a weight-decay/Adam-ε equilibrium at m*≈log(1/ε).

record.problems: The text shows only 2 of 3–5 seeds in several figures; some accuracy comparisons are given without uncertainty; the results are limited to small modular-arithmetic benchmarks. The experiments do not directly quantify the time from training-accuracy saturation to generalization or sweep training-set size.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other entries in Table 1 for Zero-sum Proj. and StableMax because they are comparator methods rather than standard or corrected cross-entropy results. Omitted margin-only measurements from Figures 2–6 because they do not measure delayed test generalization. Figure-only trajectories are represented only where the text explicitly describes their outcome.

untested.parts: Time from training-accuracy saturation to generalization is never quantified, so whether the delay shrinks to zero is not measured. Other optimizer artifacts (e.g. non-adaptive optimizers, Adam instabilities beyond the softmax cliff) are not tested.
No measurement of delay length or its dependence on training-set size.
No critical dataset size or ungrokking. The weight-decay/ε margin equilibrium is a different claim.

missing.what: Standard CE does not spike for ε≥1e-7 because log(1/ε)≤16.1<c32. This is an optimizer-hyperparameter control that removes the artifact.
Standard bf16 CE stalls at margin ~5.1–5.8 yet still reaches ~93–95% test accuracy (final-margin column of Table 1).
Test-accuracy trajectories over epochs, showing how much the grokking delay shortens with the fix. These are figure-only and never quantified in the text.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 differences have large overlapping SDs over 3–5 seeds with no significance tests. The comparator rows duplicate the main rows. Distillation (Softmax Cancellation) results are correctly excluded: they do not measure grokking.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether test accuracy rises from chance to near-perfect long after training accuracy saturates, or whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
The study does not measure formation or removal of circuits, or continuous progress measures.
The study uses algorithmic tasks and does not test non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm transitions.
The study does not test LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
The study analyzes a weight-decay/Adam epsilon equilibrium for logit margins, but does not test the efficiency-account claim, critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.
The study does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Tests numerical softmax/cross-entropy effects on grokking benchmarks, but not whether all grokking delays are artifacts, or all adaptive-optimizer and floating-point effects across training settings.

relationships.condition: Standard CE in fp32/bf16 once margins cross the precision cliff (mod 31 with λ=1; MLPs on mod 97 with λ=0)
relationships.reason: The softmax rounding bug slows and degrades grokking (94±5% vs 100±0%, slower on all seeds) and collapses accuracy without weight decay (61%→23%, 60%→21%): R19, R20, R22, R1, R7.
relationships.display_finding: Softmax rounding slowed grokking on every seed, yielded 94±5% versus 100±0% accuracy, and caused accuracy collapses from 61% to 23% and 60% to 21% without weight decay.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Standard CE in fp32/bf16 once margins cross the precision cliff (mod 31 with λ=1; MLPs on mod 97 with λ=0)
source_check.reason: R19 establishes a numerical contribution to slower grokking, not production and complete removal of the delay. R1 and R7 report endpoints; R20 and R22 report accuracy collapses. Together these support only a qualified artifact account.

relationships.condition: Fixed CE across precisions and four benchmarks
relationships.reason: With the numerical bug removed, models still grok and reach ~99–100% (described as faster), so the numerics modulate the delay rather than producing all of it. The delay itself is unquantified: R3, R5, R9, R11, R17, R24, R26, R28, R30.
relationships.display_finding: Models still grokked and reached approximately 99–100% accuracy after the correction, with faster generalization reported but no quantified delay.

source_check.condition: Fixed CE across precisions and four benchmarks
source_check.reason: Sections 4 and 6 describe grokking under corrected CE and improved convergence across benchmarks, qualifying an unrestricted artifact explanation. The listed endpoint rows do not independently establish a residual delay, and no zero-lag measurement is reported.

relationships.condition: fp64 with ε=1e-8 or 1e-12 (equilibrium margin below cliff)
relationships.reason: There is no difference between standard and fixed CE, so the artifact only acts when the ε-set margin equilibrium exceeds the precision cliff: R13, R15.
relationships.display_finding: In float64 with ε=1e-8 or 1e-12, standard and corrected cross-entropy behaved identically below the equilibrium-margin precision cliff, consistent with the artifact acting only above it.

tranche.reason: The controlled numerical interventions qualify the artifact account: correcting CE eliminates slingshot spikes and accelerates grokking without establishing disappearance of the underlying delay.

source_check.notes: Precision in Table 1 refers to logits at the loss, not necessarily all training computations. Aggregate pipeline counts and claims about other studies were outside this study-only check.

statements.correction: Table 1: standard 94.3±5.4%, fixed 100.0±0.0%; Figure 2: fixed CE groks faster on all five seeds; Sections 2–3: inline JAX implementations; no repository link stated; post-memorization lag not quantified.
statements.problem: The numerical comparison and qualitative timing claim are correct, but 'No code is reported' overlooks the implementations printed in the paper.

statements.correction: No numerical training-saturation-to-generalization interval reported; Figure 2 gives a qualitative comparison across five seeds.
statements.problem: The absence of a quantified corrected-CE lag is correct, but the paper does not explicitly list that interval as unquantified; that is the pipeline's assessment.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard cross-entropy in the reported fp32 cliff settings
reader_labels.reason: The paper attributes slingshot spikes to Softmax Collapse and reports test-accuracy drops at the cliff; see R19–R20 and R22, with additional benchmark spike results in R25, R27, R29, and R31.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Corrected cross-entropy on the reported modular benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The fix removes the numerical cliff and improves or preserves test accuracy, but the paper reports that grokking continues (and is faster), rather than showing that controlling the numerical issue eliminates grokking; these results do not establish whether the full delayed-generalization phenomenon remains.
